summary: Auth, protected routes, and public endpoints tested. 7/8 backend tests pass. All frontend route protection and public accessibility checks pass. One real backend bug found: POST /api/auth/logout only reads session_token from httpOnly cookie, not from Authorization Bearer header, so calling logout via Bearer token does NOT delete the session from MongoDB.

critical.issue: Logout only reads session_token from cookies (request.cookies.get), not from Authorization header. Calling logout with Bearer token returns 200 but session remains active in DB. Fix: also read from Authorization header and delete matching session.

action_items: Fix POST /api/auth/logout to also delete session when called with Authorization: Bearer <token> (not just cookie). In auth_logout, add: if not token: auth_header = request.headers.get('Authorization',''); token = auth_header[7:] if auth_header.startswith('Bearer ') else None
critical_code_review_comments: auth_logout (server.py line 463) only reads cookie for token deletion. Should also support Bearer token deletion for completeness, especially since other auth endpoints (auth/me) support both.

context_for_next_testing_agent: All auth-protected routes (/dashboard, /create, /checkout) correctly redirect unauthenticated users to /login. /storybook/:id, /, /admin are public. GET /api/auth/me, GET /api/stories, GET /api/orders all require auth (return 401 without token). GET /api/admin/orders requires no auth. Login page at /login has 'Welcome back' h1 and google-signin-button. The only bug is logout via Bearer token doesn't delete session. Session seeded: test_session_953a56775d6c4d5f9d08205b77377974 for user_dc377342c589 (testparent@example.com).
rca_of_the_issue: Root Cause: auth_logout reads token only from request.cookies.get('session_token'). When tested via API (Bearer header), the cookie is not present, so token=None, and the db.user_sessions.delete_one is never called. The session persists. Fix: extend the token extraction logic in auth_logout to mirror get_current_user (check cookie first, then Authorization header).
